solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Musician from Queen surrounded by supporters

indicators.note: the Queen's letters sit within the supporters, which close round them

parts.note: bras are supporting undergarments
HM stands for Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A performer from the band Queen finds himself hemmed in by fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' suggests fans, but they are BRAS; 'Queen' looks like the rock band but is HM, Her Majesty.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was a German composer, so he is an example of a musician.

clue.text: Doctor Seuss book about hot affair

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters plus the book go round the word for hot
to doctor is to tamper with, so the name Seuss is rearranged

parts.note: in means fashionable, a sense of hot

explanation.surface: A Dr Seuss book about a steamy romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Seuss' looks like the author's name, but 'Doctor' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Business means a matter or concern, as in 'a strange affair'.

clue.text: Reference is a deception — not the first one

indicators.note: not the first means the opening instance of the letter is dropped

parts.note: an illusion is a deception of the senses
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A citation turns out to be a fraud, and not the first.
explanation.definitionFit: An allusion is an indirect reference to something.

clue.text: Mark bandages leg for brother

indicators.note: a bandage wraps round, so the mark encloses the leg

parts.note: MK is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: Mark dresses his brother's injured leg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk is a member of a religious order, addressed as Brother.

clue.text: Insult outside club maybe leads to scraps

indicators.note: the insult goes round the outside of the club, holding it within

parts.note: to diss is slang for to insult
a club is one suit, so a card from it is a card, signalled by 'maybe'

explanation.surface: Abuse heaped on a nightclub ends with someone throwing things away.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap something is to throw it out, the same verb sense as discarding it.

clue.text: One with desire to eat large helping, for example

indicators.note: to eat is to take inside, so the pair swallows the letter for large

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
lust is strong desire
a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: A greedy person wanting to devour a big portion.
explanation.definitionFit: An illustration is an instance given to make a point, just as an example is.

clue.text: Am I not able to celebrate rising support?

parts.note: can't I asks whether I am not able

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means read from the bottom up

parts.note: to revel is to celebrate

explanation.surface: Someone asking why they cannot join the party for a rise in backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a projecting beam that supports a balcony or bridge.

clue.text: Evaluation is harsh, first off

indicators.note: first off says the opening letter is removed

parts.note: grating means harsh or jarring

explanation.surface: An appraisal is severe, for a start.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating is an assessment or score given to something.

clue.text: Soldier primarily positioned in front of gate?

definitions.text: Soldier primarily positioned in front of gate?

indicators.note: in a down answer this puts the single letter above the rest
primarily means only the first letter of soldier is used

parts.note: an entry is a way in, as a gate is

explanation.surface: A soldier standing at a gate, which describes the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a guard posted at an entrance, like a soldier stationed by a gate.

clue.text: Mum is regressing fast

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word 'is' is read from right to left

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Mother is going backwards quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother but means quiet; 'fast' looks like speed but is LENT, the period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep mum is to stay quiet, so mum as an adjective means saying nothing.

clue.text: They drift in the ocean, not going back on board

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: a plank is a long board of wood

indicators.note: going back says the word 'not' is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Castaways cling to a plank at sea, refusing to return.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are tiny organisms carried by currents rather than swimming, so they drift in the sea.

clue.text: Sponsor has complaint about new performer

indicators.note: the complaint goes about, enclosing the letter for new

parts.note: a beef is slang for a grievance
an actress is a stage performer

explanation.surface: A backer grumbles about a fresh actor in the cast.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactress is a woman who gives financial support, a patron.

clue.text: Retreat from scene, staggering somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone backs away from an incident, rather unsteady on their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is a cosy hideaway, a place of retreat.

clue.text: Bowler hat shunned by scruffy English parent

indicators.note: the letters of the word hat are kept out of the mix, avoided by the rest
scruffy means untidy, so the letters of English parent are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bowler hat is snubbed by a shabby English mother or father.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle ENGLISH PARENT with the letters of HAT taken out ('shunned by'); 'scruffy' is the anagram signal. 'Bowler hat' is a red herring: the definition is just 'Bowler'.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a leg-spinner is a type of slow bowler who spins the ball from leg to off.

clue.text: Writing articles still for The Listener

indicators.note: for a listener means the word is heard rather than read, so its sound counts

parts.note: stationary means still, not moving

explanation.surface: Pens and paper still supplied for a magazine called The Listener.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener was a BBC magazine, making the homophone signal look like a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationery covers paper, envelopes and pens, the materials for writing.

clue.text: Brave, like pugilist outwardly?

parts.note: the last two letters of pugilist and the first three of outwardly together spell a word for portly, sitting at the heart of the phrase

explanation.surface: Courageous, as a boxer appears from the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as instructions: STOUT placed at the heart. The phrase 'pugilist outwardly' has STOUT in its middle, so it is 'stout-hearted', hence 'like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a stout heart has courage, so the compound adjective means valiant.

clue.text: In the right over lost exotic bird

indicators.note: In says the following pieces go inside the word 'the'
in a down answer over puts the letter above the next piece
exotic means strange, so the letters of lost are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusual bird lost somewhere on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: The throstle is a poetic name for the song thrush, a bird.

clue.text: Conman from Cornwall perhaps less active around November

parts.note: Cornwall is in the South West of England, SW, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example

indicators.note: around means the lazier word goes round the letter for November

parts.note: idler means lazier, less active
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A trickster from Cornwall slows down around November.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is a county in South West England.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler is a cheat or fraudster, the same as a con artist.

clue.text: To get the best hand towels, he has to wander around Tunisia's capital

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the single letter picked from the country
letters made to wander are moved about into a new order
capital here means the first letter of Tunisia

explanation.surface: A towel-related errand around Tunis, oddly framed as a way to win.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal the show is to win the most applause at a performance, a 'hand' being a round of clapping.

clue.text: Paris shuffled last off mortal coil

indicators.note: shuffled means the letters of Paris are mixed up
the last letter taken off the word mortal

explanation.surface: Paris shuffled off this mortal coil, echoing Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows Hamlet's 'shuffled off this mortal coil'; the definition is just 'coil'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral is a winding shape, the same as a coil.

clue.text: Toff's after top of range? Hang about!

indicators.note: after puts the toff below the cooker part in this down answer

parts.note: a hob is the cooking surface on top of a range cooker
nob is slang for a toff, an upper-class person

explanation.surface: An aristocrat chasing the best of the range is told to wait.
explanation.walkthrough: A range is a large kitchen stove; its top is the hob.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to mix socially, to hang about with people.

clue.text: Support playwright nursing one relation

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the playwright holds the numeral inside

parts.note: Joe Orton was an English playwright
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dramatist being propped up while caring for a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Orton wrote the 1960s black comedies Loot and Entertaining Mr Sloane.
explanation.definitionFit: Proportion means a ratio or relation of one quantity to another.

clue.text: New online community member returns gift

indicators.note: returns means the word for a newcomer is read backwards

parts.note: a noob is internet slang for a newcomer to an online game or forum

explanation.surface: A newcomer to a forum sends back a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a blessing or benefit, something given as a favour.

clue.text: Capital punishment

definitions.meaning: capital as an old-fashioned word for excellent

explanation.surface: The death penalty, as a single phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine means first-rate, like capital, and also a monetary penalty.

clue.text: Aim to stop case of Rhine wine getting delivered

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so the aim goes into the space between the outside letters
the case is the outer shell, here the first and last letters of Rhine

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
red is a type of wine

explanation.surface: A goal of corking a crate of German wine being handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendered can mean handed over or given, as in services rendered.

clue.text: Pilot's shot — using this?

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or broken, so the letters of Pilot's are scrambled

explanation.surface: An airman takes a shot and we wonder what weapon he used.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: a pilot taking a shot might use a handgun.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol is a handgun, the thing one fires when taking a shot.

clue.text: Campaigner has inclination to grab 'Arry's interest

indicators.note: the inclination grabs the interest, holding it inside

parts.note: a list is a lean or tilt, as of a ship
hobby, said in a Cockney accent that drops the H as in 'Arry for Harry

explanation.surface: A campaigner tends to latch onto Harry's pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Arry signals the dropped H, so 'interest' (hobby) loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobbyist campaigns to influence lawmakers on behalf of a cause.

clue.text: The woman's turned attention to judge again

indicators.note: turned means the possessive is reversed

parts.note: her is the possessive meaning the woman's
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A woman turns her attention to a judge once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehear a case is to try it a second time in court.
